title: Order-invariance — 11 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
Order-invariance. 11 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/quantum.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. All are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). One further declaration closes by rfl, checked by evaluation, and is not included here, by design. Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 5 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 32 pairs; the theorems fall into 2 strands, the largest of 8. Most binding: perms (7), receipt (4), ghzXSupport (3), naive (2), par3 (2).

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 1 file: src/proof/quantum.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 11 sealed receipts fold to 18d30f2b-d336-8caf-9a47-146ae047dfc4. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (8, 1, 0, 3, 3, 7, 7). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: elementary.lean (9 observed, 3.82 expected, lift 2.36), address.lean (5 observed, 2.39 expected, lift 2.09), energy.lean (4 observed, 2.67 expected, lift 1.5). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 2.85 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 81.5% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 16.18; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.53. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 7b6ebaaa9854 (2026-09-15), over 807 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. Sorting a multiset into a canonical order BEFORE folding it is standard practice, not a discovery here. Sorted-leaf Merkle trees are the recommended construction for multiproofs and are shipped that way in OpenZeppelin's merkle-tree library; canonical ordering before hashing is long-established in cryptographic serialisation generally. The mathematical content is elementary: any function of a canonical form is invariant under permutation of its input, which is why receipt_is_order_invariant holds. What this file contributes is the Lean verification over a stated finite domain and the negative controls beside it — naive_fold_is_not_order_invariant shows the property is bought by the sort and not free, and the_receipt_is_not_injective and the_invariance_is_canonicalisation_not_physics state its limits. Verification and refusal, not discovery. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. perms_of_four_is_factorial — (perms [1, 2, 4, 8]).length = 24 record
  2. receipt_is_order_invariant — (perms [1, 2, 4, 8]).all (fun p => receipt p == receipt [1, 2, 4, 8]) record
  3. receipt_order_invariant_on_the_orbit — (perms [1, 2, 4, 8, 7, 5]).all (fun p => receipt p == receipt [1, 2, 4, 8, 7, 5]) record
  4. naive_fold_is_not_order_invariant — ¬ ((perms [1, 2, 4, 8]).all (fun p => naive p == naive [1, 2, 4, 8])) record
  5. superposition_collapses_to_one — ((perms [1, 2, 4, 8]).map receipt).eraseDups.length = 1 record
  6. the_invariance_is_canonicalisation_not_physics — (perms [1, 2, 4, 8]).all (fun p => sort p == sort [1, 2, 4, 8]) record
  7. the_receipt_is_not_injective — pairsOverNine.length = 45 ∧ (pairsOverNine.map receipt).eraseDups.length = 9 record
  8. the_uncanonicalised_fold_gives_many_answers — ((perms [1, 2, 4, 8]).map naive).eraseDups.length = 5 record
  9. the_ghz_x_support_is_exactly_the_even_parity_strings — (List.range 8).filter (fun n => par3 n == 0) = ghzXSupport record
  10. it_is_half_of_the_eight — ghzXSupport.length = 4 ∧ (List.range 8).length = 8 record
  11. a_classical_mixture_reaches_the_parity_ghz_never_does — ((List.range 8).filter (fun n => par3 n == 1)).length = 4 ∧ ((List.range 8).filter (fun n => par3 n == 1)).all (fun n => ¬ ghzXSupport.contains n) record
